title: Beyond the 956: Tommy Mars, Frank Zappa's keyboardist, dies at 75
excerpt: Tommy Mars, the keyboardist who played with Frank Zappa from 1977 to 1984 and appeared on albums including Sheik Yerbouti and You Are What You Is, has died at 75. His death was announced November 19 by longtime bandmate Arthur Barrow; no cause of death was disclosed.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Tommy Mars, the keyboardist who spent seven years in Frank Zappa's band and helped shape the sound of some of Zappa's best-known records, has died at 75.

Mars died November 19, 2026. His death was announced that day by longtime Zappa bandmate Arthur Barrow, who wrote on social media: “I am sorry to say that the great Tommy Mars passed away. He was a great musician and a good friend. Rest in peace Tommy.” No cause of death was disclosed.

Born Thomas Mariano on October 26, 1951, Mars joined Zappa's band in 1977 and remained with the group until 1984. He contributed keyboards to albums including Sheik Yerbouti and You Are What You Is, as well as the 1979 film Baby Snakes.

Barrow, who played bass alongside Mars in Zappa's band, was among those paying tribute, calling Mars one of the best keyboardists Zappa ever had.

Sources: Page Six; American Songwriter; Ultimate Classic Rock; Far Out; Arthur Barrow.
